Label: Dhanteras
Hook: Tonight we buy a little gold, or a new steel pot, for luck.
Sub: This year, add one thing that costs nothing: look at your money with attention.
Does: Luck can't be planned.
Attention can start tonight.
What you look at, you start to look after.
Line: I give my money attention, and it grows in my care.
LineHi: मेरा ध्यान मेरे धन की देखभाल करता है।
ActHead: Write three numbers on paper.
ActBody: What came in last month, what went out, what is left. Real figures. No judging.
Question: What did your family buy on Dhanteras when you were a child?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Sub: Money is just dirt on your hands. It was meant to keep us humble. Your bank balance heard it too.
Does: It makes saving feel greedy.
It makes asking for a raise feel shameful.
It makes the money leave before the 20th.
Line: I can respect money and still stay humble.
LineHi: पैसे का सम्मान और विनम्रता, दोनों मेरे साथ हैं।
ActHead: Open your UPI history for this week.
ActBody: Find one spend you didn't enjoy. Don't fix it, don't judge it. Just notice it. Noticing is where respect starts.
Question: Who in your family used to say this?

Label: Diwali
Hook: We clean every corner so Lakshmi feels welcome.
Sub: Your money has corners too: the forgotten subscription, the account you never check.
Does: Small leaks hide behind big festivals.
Unopened statements turn into quiet worry.
A clean money life feels lighter to look at.
Line: I welcome wealth into a clean, clear home.
LineHi: साफ़ और सुलझे घर में धन का स्वागत है।
ActHead: Cancel one subscription you forgot about.
ActBody: Check your UPI autopay list or card statement. One is enough for tonight.
Question: Which money corner needs cleaning this Diwali?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Sub: Wealth is restless and never stays. We say it after every bonus that vanished.
Does: It makes losing money feel like fate.
It makes a plan feel pointless.
It turns every windfall into a spending spree.
Line: Money stays longer where it has a plan.
LineHi: जहाँ योजना है, वहाँ धन टिकता है।
ActHead: Give your next salary a job before it arrives.
ActBody: Split it on paper into needs, savings and joy. Three lines are enough.
Question: Have you heard this said after money disappeared?

Label: Salary day
Hook: Credited on the 1st. Gone by the 20th.
Sub: No big purchase. Just a hundred small taps on UPI.
Does: Small spends don't feel like spending.
The balance falls without a single decision.
By month-end, worry fills the gap.
Line: Every rupee I earn finds its purpose.
LineHi: मेरी कमाई का हर रुपया अपना काम जानता है।
ActHead: Move a fixed amount aside on salary day.
ActBody: Before any spend. Even ₹500. The habit matters more than the amount.
Question: Which day of the month does your salary usually run out?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Hook: “Jitni chadar ho, utne hi pair phailao.”
HookHi: जितनी चादर हो, उतने ही पैर फैलाओ।
Sub: Stretch your legs only as far as your sheet. Good advice, but only half of it.
Does: Right: don't spend beyond what you have.
Left out: you can also grow the sheet.
Living small forever isn't the only safe choice.
Line: I live within my means, and I grow my means.
LineHi: चादर में रहना और चादर बढ़ाना, दोनों मेरे हाथ में हैं।
ActHead: Write one skill that could raise your income.
ActBody: Not a dream. One skill, and the first free step to learn it.
Question: Right now, is your sheet too small or are your legs too long?

Label: The costliest question
Sub: The most expensive question in Indian families.
Does: It doubles the wedding budget.
It buys the bigger car for the neighbours.
It keeps loans running long after the photos.
Line: I spend for my life, not for an audience.
LineHi: मेरा खर्च मेरी ज़िंदगी के लिए है, दिखावे के लिए नहीं।
ActHead: Name one spend you made mainly for others to see.
ActBody: Just name it. Seeing it clearly is how the next one gets smaller.
Question: What's one thing you bought because of log kya kahenge?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Sub: What's at home is never valued. That includes your own work.
DoesLabel: Where it shows up at work
Does: You do extra and call it “nothing much”.
You price your work low to seem polite.
People notice your value only after you leave.
Line: I see my own value clearly, and I say it.
LineHi: अपनी क़ीमत मुझे साफ़ दिखती है, और उसे कहना मेरा हक़ है।
ActHead: List three things you did this month that saved someone time or money.
ActBody: Keep the list. It's your appraisal script.
Question: Where in your life are you the ghar ki murgi?

Label: Family and money
Sub: A loan is the scissors of love. Every family has a story.
DoesLabel: Why lending to family gets messy
Does: Nobody says the amount or the date out loud.
Asking for it back feels like an insult.
The money and the relationship both go quiet.
Line: I can love my family and protect my savings.
LineHi: परिवार से प्यार और अपनी बचत की हिफ़ाज़त, दोनों साथ चल सकते हैं।
ActHead: Decide your family-help limit before anyone asks.
ActBody: A number you can give without needing it back. Above that, you say no kindly.
Question: Have you ever lost money, or a friendship, to udhaar?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Money saved is money earned. Our grandparents lived by it.
Does: A rupee saved needs no boss and no overtime.
Savings turn emergencies into inconveniences.
A small cushion makes you braver at work.
Line: My savings give me calm and courage.
LineHi: मेरी बचत मुझे सुकून भी देती है और हिम्मत भी।
ActHead: Pick one regular spend and cut it by half this week.
ActBody: Not to zero, just half. Put the difference aside and watch it.
Question: What did your grandparents save on that you still do?

Label: Appraisal season
Hook: Your manager asks, “What are you expecting?”
Sub: And you say, “Whatever you think is fair.”
Does: It hands your number to someone else.
It signals you haven't thought about your worth.
The gap repeats every year after.
Line: I can say my number calmly.
LineHi: अपनी माँग शांति से रखना मुझे आता है।
ActHead: Find the market range for your role.
ActBody: Ask two people in your field, or read ten job posts. Write the range down.
Question: Have you ever named your number in an appraisal?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Drop by drop, an ocean fills. The oldest money lesson we have.
Does: ₹100 a day feels like nothing.
It is ₹36,500 a year.
The habit grows before the number does.
Line: Small steady steps build my wealth.
LineHi: छोटे पर लगातार क़दम मेरा धन बनाते हैं।
ActHead: Pick a daily amount you can set aside without pain.
ActBody: ₹50 or ₹100. Start tomorrow. Doing it every day is the whole trick.
Question: What will your daily boond be?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Something's off. Say it whenever a money offer sounds too good.
Does: “Guaranteed” returns, and fast.
Pressure to decide today.
A friend earns only if you join.
Line: I stay calm when an offer sounds too good.
LineHi: बहुत अच्छे लगने वाले ऑफ़र के सामने भी मेरा मन शांत रहता है।
ActHead: Don't decide on any money offer tonight.
ActBody: Sleep on every one. A real opportunity will still be there tomorrow.
Question: Have you or someone you know been caught by a too-good scheme?

Label: Kabir
Hook: “Kaal kare so aaj kar, aaj kare so ab.”
HookHi: काल करे सो आज कर, आज करे सो अब।
Sub: Do tomorrow's work today, and today's work now.
Does: The bill you avoid opening keeps growing.
The form you'll fill “next week” stays blank.
Worry runs in the background all month.
Line: I handle money tasks now, not later.
LineHi: पैसे का काम आज और अभी, कल पर नहीं।
ActHead: Do one money task you've been avoiding.
ActBody: Under ten minutes. Pay one bill, check one statement, or add one nominee.
Question: Which money task have you been putting off?

Label: A saying we grew up with
HookHi: मुफ़्त का चंदन, घिस मेरे नंदन।
Sub: Free sandalwood gets rubbed away. What costs nothing, we waste.
Does: Free delivery makes you add things you didn't need.
Free trials quietly turn into paid plans.
Cashback makes you spend in order to save.
Line: I buy what I need, not what's on offer.
LineHi: मेरी ख़रीद मेरी ज़रूरत से तय होती है, ऑफ़र से नहीं।
ActHead: Move one shopping app off your home screen.
ActBody: Just for a week. Notice how often your thumb goes looking for it.
Question: Which “free” offer tempts you most?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Greed is a curse. Every childhood story ended with this line.
Does: “Double your money in a month.”
Copying a trade from a reel.
Borrowing to chase what others made.
Line: I grow my money patiently.
LineHi: धीरज से धन बढ़ता है, और मुझमें धीरज है।
ActHead: Unfollow one account that promises fast money.
ActBody: Your feed shapes your patience. Make it a calmer place.
Question: What's the fastest-money promise you've seen this month?

Label: Family and money
Hook: You're the first earner, and everyone looks to you.
Sub: Pride, love and pressure, all in one bank account.
Does: You say yes before checking your balance.
Your own goals keep moving to “next year”.
Guilt follows every rupee you spend on yourself.
Line: Caring for my family includes caring for myself.
LineHi: परिवार की देखभाल में अपनी देखभाल भी शामिल है।
ActHead: Write one goal that is only for you.
ActBody: A course, a trip, a cushion. Give it a small monthly amount.
Question: Are you the main earner in your family?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Your own hands are your god. What you do yourself gets done.
Does: Nobody else will track your spending.
Nobody else will ask for your raise.
Small habits you build beat big promises.
Line: My own hands build my security.
LineHi: मेरी सुरक्षा मेरे अपने हाथों से बनती है।
ActHead: Set a weekly 15-minute money date with yourself.
ActBody: Same day, same time. Check your balance, your spends and one goal.
Question: Which day works for your money date?

Label: A saying we grew up with
Hook: “Ab pachhtaye hot kya, jab chidiya chug gayi khet.”
HookHi: अब पछताए होत क्या, जब चिड़िया चुग गई खेत।
Sub: What's the use of regret once the birds have eaten the field?
Does: The emergency fund we meant to start.
The cover we would “get later”.
The hospital bill that arrived first.
Line: I prepare today for the days I can't see.
LineHi: आज की तैयारी, कल के अनदेखे दिनों के लिए।
ActHead: Start an emergency envelope, however small.
ActBody: One place, one rule: only for real emergencies.
Question: What did an emergency once teach you about money?

Label: EMI
Sub: No-cost EMI makes everything sound small.
Does: Small monthly numbers hide big totals.
Three EMIs together become a second rent.
Next year's salary is spent before it arrives.
Line: I decide by the full price, not the monthly one.
LineHi: फ़ैसला पूरी क़ीमत देखकर, किस्त देखकर नहीं।
ActHead: Add up all your current EMIs.
ActBody: One total, one line. Put it next to your monthly salary.
Question: How many EMIs are you running right now?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: Truth fears no fire. Honest work holds up.
Does: You never need to remember a lie.
Trust brings repeat work and referrals.
You sleep well on what you earned.
Line: I earn with honesty, and it lasts.
LineHi: ईमानदारी की कमाई टिकती है, और मेरी कमाई ईमानदार है।
ActHead: Thank one client, boss or customer by name.
ActBody: A short, honest message. Relationships are where income repeats.
Question: Who trusted you with work early on?

Label: Comparison
Hook: A school friend posts a new car. Your mood drops.
Sub: Their highlights against your behind-the-scenes.
Does: You feel behind in a race you never entered.
You spend to catch up.
Your own progress becomes invisible.
Line: My money grows at my own pace.
LineHi: मेरा धन मेरी अपनी रफ़्तार से बढ़ता है।
ActHead: Write how you're better off than three years ago.
ActBody: One honest line. Progress you don't measure doesn't feel real.
Question: What do you have now that you didn't three years ago?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: If there's life, there's a world. Health comes first.
DoesLabel: Why health is a money matter
Does: Every income plan assumes a working body.
One hospital week can undo a year of saving.
A tired mind makes costly choices.
Line: Caring for my health protects my wealth.
LineHi: सेहत का ख़याल ही धन की हिफ़ाज़त है।
ActHead: Do one thing today for the body that earns.
ActBody: A walk, an early night, or the check-up you keep postponing.
Question: What's your one health promise this week?

Label: Money silence
Hook: At home, money was never discussed in front of the children.
Sub: So we learned it by guessing.
Does: Money feels secret, even shameful.
We repeat habits we never chose.
We don't ask for help when we need it.
Line: I can talk about money openly and calmly.
LineHi: पैसे पर खुलकर और शांति से बात करना ठीक है।
ActHead: Ask one elder how they handled money at your age.
ActBody: Listen for one lesson to keep and one to leave behind.
Question: Was money talked about in your home?

Label: A belief we grew up with
Sub: The safest job is a government job. Many of us heard little else.
Does: Skills that people will pay for.
Savings that cover a bad year.
More than one source of income.
Line: My skills and savings keep me safe.
LineHi: मेरा हुनर और मेरी बचत, यही मेरी सुरक्षा है।
ActHead: Write down every source of income you have.
ActBody: Salary, freelance, rent, interest. Even ₹500 counts.
Question: What did your parents think was the “safe” career?

Label: Spending on yourself
Hook: You bought something for yourself. Then felt guilty all evening.
Sub: Many of us were taught that wanting is selfish.
Does: You overspend on others to balance it.
Joy money gets spent in secret.
Unplanned treats surprise your budget.
Line: Planned joy is part of a good money life.
LineHi: सोची-समझी ख़ुशी भी अच्छी आर्थिक ज़िंदगी का हिस्सा है।
ActHead: Give yourself a small monthly joy amount.
ActBody: Planned, guilt-free and yours. When it's used, it's used.
Question: What small thing would you love to buy without guilt?

Label: A saying worth keeping
Sub: As you do, so you receive.
Does: This year's habits are next year's balance.
Careless small spends add up quietly.
So do careful small choices.
Line: Today's small choices shape my future wealth.
LineHi: आज के छोटे फ़ैसले मेरे कल का धन बनाते हैं।
ActHead: Write tomorrow's one money choice tonight.
ActBody: One line: what you'll skip, save or do.
Question: Which habit from last year shows in your money today?

Label: Saying no
Hook: A friend plans an expensive trip. You say yes, then regret it.
Sub: Saying no feels rude. Saying yes costs you for months.
Does: You fund plans you didn't choose.
Resentment grows quietly.
Your own goals wait again.
Line: I can say no kindly and keep my plans.
LineHi: प्यार से “ना” कहना और अपनी योजना पर टिके रहना, दोनों मुमकिन हैं।
ActHead: Practise one kind no.
ActBody: “That's not in my budget this month, but let's plan something soon.”
Question: What's the hardest money no you've had to say?

Label: Your numbers
Hook: Do you know what you spent last month? Roughly?
Sub: Most of us guess, and we guess low.
Does: The imagined number is scarier than the real one.
You can't fix what you can't see.
Worry fills the space the numbers should.
Line: I know my numbers, and they don't scare me.
LineHi: अपने आँकड़े मुझे पता हैं, और अब उनसे डर नहीं लगता।
ActHead: Download last month's bank statement.
ActBody: Add up the total spent. One number. That's all for tonight.
Question: Did the number surprise you?

Label: Night 30
Hook: Thirty nights of lines. What's different?
Sub: Not your bank balance yet. Maybe how you look at it.
DoesLabel: What a month of attention does
Does: You notice spends before they happen.
You say your number more easily.
Money feels less like a secret.
Line: I am becoming calm and clear with money.
LineHi: पैसे के साथ मेरा रिश्ता शांत और साफ़ हो रहा है।
ActHead: Write one change you've noticed in thirty nights.
ActBody: Keep it. You'll read it again on night ninety.
Question: What's one change you've noticed?
